vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: extract-memories
Version: 3.0.7

The skill 'extract-memories' is designed to summarize conversation history and persist key information into a structured memory system (markdown files). It requests standard permissions for its purpose, such as FileRead, FileWrite, and sessions_history, and includes explicit safety guidelines ('What NOT to Save') to prevent the storage of sensitive technical data like source code or Git history. No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or obfuscation were found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: This instruction-only skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose: it reads conversation context and writes curated “memory” topic files under memory/, and it does not request unrelated credentials or installs.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description match the actions it specifies: extracting conversation content and persisting topic files under memory/. Requested permissions (file read/write and session history) are appropriate for this purpose and no unrelated env vars or binaries are required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs reading the main session history and writing topic files and an index (MEMORY.md). Those actions are within scope, but they involve reading potentially sensitive conversation content and making persistent edits. The skill also suggests adding a line to AGENTS.md for integration (integration guidance, not a hard requirement).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files — this is instruction-only, so nothing is downloaded or written by an installer. That minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables or external credentials. The only privileges it requests are file read/write/edit for memory/ and access to sessions_history, which are proportionate to persisting extracted memories.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (normal). disable-model-invocation is false so the agent can autonomously trigger extraction (as intended). This autonomy combined with file write access means the agent can automatically add persistent records at conversation end; users should be aware and control triggers if needed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears coherent and does what it says: automatically extract and save conversation 'memories' into memory/topics/ and update MEMORY.md. Before enabling it, consider: 

- Review and control the memory/ directory: ensure it is the intended storage location and not a sensitive system path. 
- Sensitive content risk: the skill reads full session history; decide whether you want conversational content persisted and adjust triggers (disable automatic heartbeat/auto-run or require manual /extract-memories). 
- Least privilege: grant only the minimal FileRead/FileWrite access it needs (memory/ and MEMORY.md), and avoid giving it access to other directories. 
- Review generated files regularly and add retention or deletion policies for sensitive entries. 
- Ensure heartbeat-state.json is created per the README if you rely on heartbeat triggers. 

If you want stronger guarantees, require manual invocation only or add a confirmation step before writing any memory flagged as potentially sensitive.
